reach_towns.label: Release 2 · Earth-calibrated sizes · sliding 100–500 people/ha
reach_towns.note: Release 2: town SIZES calibrated on Earth, on the existing town positions. Built-up areas follow the official catalogue of Roman cities (Hanson 2016): held-out distribution distance 0.058 against a 0.10 limit. Residents = area × sliding 100–500 people/ha, a density scenario, not a census: 13.49 M town residents, 25.4% of the world's people, largest 255,326. Which place is large is almost unexplained on Earth, so the largest sizes are given to the campaign's marked capital, cities and fortified towns (a lore choice). Every resident is taken from surrounding rural cells; nobody is created. Only 245 of 1034 towns (white centre) could be fed from one day's local grain collection in the central scenario; the rest depend on wider supply. Town positions were NOT changed: the tested new placement rule won 5 of 8 regions, short of its declared 6. Reach, trade and administration layers still use the earlier settlement sizes.
